source_read: PDF, pp. 1–5 (all pages; article 103065, pages unnumbered and counted from the first page; Table 1 checked on rendered p. 2, Figs. 1–2 on rendered pp. 3–4, Fig. 1C at higher resolution; supplementary material not available)

claims.overstatement: None in substance. Two wording points: (1) 'read once' is not stated in the main text (Table 1 gives one grade per cell and no replicates are described; the supplement was not seen), so 'no replicates reported' is safer; (2) 'carfentanil gave at most a faint band at 1000 ng/mL' is easy to misread with these competitive strips, where the band fades as the drug rises: at 1000 ng/mL the reading was weak positive or ambiguous (faint test band) on three brands and negative (solid band) on One Step.
claims.note: Recount from Table 1 (++/+ positive): 100 ng/mL 5, 5, 12, 9 of the 23 measured (Rapid Response, Rapid Self Test, One Step, Nal van Minden); 1000 ng/mL 21, 19, 15, 22 of 28; cumulative to 10 000 ng/mL 24, 24, 21, 24 of 28: same as the paper's summary rows and the claim. The Negative row at 100 ng/mL (15, 19, 14, 13) counts the five compounds not measured there as negative. Makers' rule (++ only), my recount: 1, 2, 11, 4 at 100 ng/mL and 20, 20, 19, 21 cumulative: same as the claim. Carfentanil was made at 4000, not 10 000 ng/mL (Methods), although the Discussion says 4000–10 000 ng/mL.

anchors.locator: Table 1, summary rows and footnote a
anchors.extracted: Clearly positive or positive (++/+): Rapid Response 5 / 21 / 24, Rapid Self Test 5 / 19 / 24, One Step 12 / 15 / 21, Nal van Minden 9 / 22 / 24 at 100, 1000 and (cumulative, 1000 plus 10 000) 10 000 ng/mL; five compounds not measured at 100 ng/mL. Editors' recount of ++ only: 1, 2, 11, 4 at 100 ng/mL; 20, 20, 19, 21 cumulative.

anchors.locator: Table 1, rows alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl, norcarfentanil, carfentanil; footnote b
anchors.extracted: Alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl and norcarfentanil negative on all four brands at 1000 and 10 000 ng/mL. Carfentanil at 1000 ng/mL: weak positive/ambiguous (faint T-band) on three brands, negative on One Step; at 4000 ng/mL clearly positive on all brands except One Step.

anchors.locator: Results › Sensitivity of fentanyl test strips, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: No strip positive for carfentanil at 1000 ng/mL; Rapid Response, Rapid Self Test and Nal van Minden positive at 4000 ng/mL or more; One Step negative at all concentrations tested.

anchors.locator: Results › Additive effect of fentanyl analogues for test strip results, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Acetylfentanyl, acrylfentanyl, furanylfentanyl and butyrfentanyl at 10 ng/mL each: negative or weak positive/ambiguous alone; a mixture of the four (each 10 ng/mL) read positive; tested on Nal van Minden only; authors expect the effect for all brands (untested).

anchors.locator: Methods › Preparation of drug solutions for fentanyl test strip experiments; Methods › Fentanyl test strip experiments
anchors.extracted: Single-component solutions in Type 1 water at 100 and 1000 ng/mL, 10 000 ng/mL for selected analogues and 4000 ng/mL for carfentanil; strips dipped 13–20 s per the urine instructions; number of strips per solution and who read them not stated in the main text.

anchors.locator: Results › Interpretation of test results, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Makers' rule: negative whenever two bands appear, whatever the test-band intensity. Because results were strongly concentration dependent (10–250 ng/mL), the authors graded four levels (++ no T-band, + barely visible, (+) faint, − solid) and counted ++/+ as positive.

anchors.locator: Discussion, 2nd paragraph; Conclusion
anchors.extracted: Three brands positive for 19–22 of 28 analogues at 1000 ng/mL and 24 at 10 000 ng/mL, One Step 15 and 21; authors conclude the strips detect the vast majority of analogues on the recreational market, a generalization from a 28-compound panel mostly read at 1000 ng/mL or more.

claims.note: Table 1 confirms One Step negative for carfentanil (100, 1000 and 4000 ng/mL), sufentanil (1000 and 10 000) and benzodioxolefentanyl (100, 1000, 10 000), each detected by the other three brands (benzodioxolefentanyl at 1000, carfentanil at 4000, sufentanil + at 10 000). One Step was also the most sensitive brand at 100 ng/mL. Fig. 2 shows the ascorbic-acid levels tested were 0, 1.5, 10, 25 and 75 mg/mL.

anchors.locator: Results › Sensitivity of fentanyl test strips, 1st paragraph; Table 1 (p. 2)
anchors.extracted: At 100 ng/mL (5–10 times the listed cut-offs) positive analogues: One Step 12, Rapid Response 5, Rapid Self Test 5, Nal van Minden 9.

anchors.locator: Results › Selectivity of fentanyl test strips, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Rapid Response, Rapid Self Test and Nal van Minden had identical selectivity (all analogues except alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl, norcarfentanil, and remifentanil only weak/ambiguous); One Step also negative for benzodioxolefentanyl, carfentanil, remifentanil and sufentanil.

anchors.locator: Results › The effect of ascorbic acid and heroin on test results, 2nd paragraph; Fig. 2
anchors.extracted: Drug-free ascorbic acid 0–75 mg/mL: 10–75 mg/mL gave false positives on One Step only; no effect at 1.5 mg/mL; the other three brands unaffected.

anchors.locator: Methods › Fentanyl test strips
anchors.extracted: Four brands from four makers (Canada two, Germany, China); listed urine cut-offs 20 ng/mL (Rapid Response, Rapid Self Test, One Step) and 10 ng/mL (Nal van Minden).

anchors.locator: Fig. 1C
anchors.extracted: One fentanyl dilution series per brand: Rapid Response ++ at 250 and 100, + at 50, (+) at 25, − at 10 ng/mL; One Step ++ at 250, 100 and 50, + at 25, (+) at 10 ng/mL: brands differ for fentanyl itself.

claims.overstatement: Accurate for Table 1 but incomplete: Fig. 1C (p. 3) shows lower positive readings for two brands (authors' rule: Rapid Response from 50 ng/mL, One Step from 25 ng/mL; makers' rule: 100 and 50 ng/mL), and it grades Rapid Response '++' at 100 ng/mL where Table 1 has '+', so the paper itself gives two different readings at that concentration. 'Single readings' is not stated in the main text.
claims.note: Table 1 fentanyl row recounted: 100 ng/mL Rapid Response +, Rapid Self Test +, One Step ++, Nal van Minden ++; ++ on all at 1000 ng/mL.

anchors.locator: Table 1, row Fentanyl
anchors.extracted: Fentanyl at 100 ng/mL: + (barely visible T-band) on Rapid Response and Rapid Self Test, ++ (no T-band) on One Step and Nal van Minden; ++ on all at 1000 ng/mL; 10 000 not measured.

anchors.locator: Fig. 1C
anchors.extracted: Descending fentanyl series (250, 100, 50, 25, 10, 0 ng/mL): Rapid Response ++, ++, +, (+), −, −; One Step ++, ++, ++, +, (+), −. Lowest positive (++/+) 50 and 25 ng/mL; Rapid Response at 100 ng/mL graded ++ here against + in Table 1.

anchors.locator: Results › Interpretation of test results, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Readings strongly concentration dependent over 10–250 ng/mL; the makers' rule counts any visible test band as negative.

anchors.locator: Discussion, 3rd paragraph; Conclusion
anchors.extracted: Testing by adding water to used equipment gives much more dilute solutions; authors recommend testing injection solutions without further dilution and reading a faint T-band as presence.

claims.overstatement: None in the statement. In the magnitude, 'heroin 50 000 ng/mL no effect' should say that heroin was tested only as a background to fentanyl, carfentanil and remifentanil at 1000 ng/mL, not alone; and the twelve drugs were tested only at 100 and 1000 ng/mL (at most 0.001 mg/mL), which says nothing about the mg/mL concentrations at which other studies found false positives (the claim does give the concentrations).
claims.note: Twelve non-fentanyl drugs: U-47700, U-48800, U-50488, methadone, amphetamine, cocaine, heroin, LSD, MDMA, methamphetamine, morphine, THC.

anchors.locator: Results › Selectivity of fentanyl test strips, 2nd paragraph; Methods › Preparation of drug solutions (p. 2)
anchors.extracted: All four brands negative for U-47700, U-48800, U-50488, methadone, amphetamine, cocaine, heroin, LSD, MDMA, methamphetamine, morphine and THC, each made at 100 and 1000 ng/mL in Type 1 water.

anchors.locator: Results › The effect of ascorbic acid and heroin on test results, 2nd paragraph; Fig. 2
anchors.extracted: Drug-free ascorbic acid at 10–75 mg/mL read positive on One Step only; diluted to 1.5 mg/mL it had no effect; no other brand affected.

anchors.locator: Results › The effect of ascorbic acid and heroin on test results, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Fentanyl, carfentanil and remifentanil (1000 ng/mL) in ascorbic acid 75 mg/mL or heroin 50 000 ng/mL: results unchanged, except One Step now clearly positive for carfentanil and remifentanil in ascorbic acid; heroin had no effect on any brand.

claims.overstatement: None. The band-to-concentration relation was shown only in pure fentanyl solutions near the cut-off: in Fig. 1C the band is already gone (++) from 100 ng/mL (Rapid Response) or 50 ng/mL (One Step), so at the concentrations of a dissolved drug sample its strength could not show how much drug is present, which supports the claim's point.

anchors.locator: Results › Interpretation of test results, 1st paragraph; Fig. 1A and 1C
anchors.extracted: Makers' instructions: negative if two bands appear regardless of test-band intensity. In fentanyl solutions the test band weakened as concentration rose from 10 to 250 ng/mL, disappearing from 100 ng/mL (Rapid Response) or 50 ng/mL (One Step).

anchors.locator: Table 1 (alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl, norcarfentanil, carfentanil); Abstract › Conclusions
anchors.extracted: Three analogues never detected and carfentanil only at 4000 ng/mL on three brands; authors: strips are no panacea because certain analogues are not detected.

anchors.locator: Discussion, 3rd paragraph
anchors.extracted: Adding water to used equipment, as web shops and harm-reduction groups advise, dilutes the drug and raises the chance of a negative strip for potentially deadly carfentanil amounts.

key_findings.correction: Matches my reading of Fig. 1C at higher resolution, including the Table 1 / Fig. 1C difference at 100 ng/mL.
Recounted: 4-fluoroisobutyr-, acetyl-, acryl- and methoxyacetylfentanyl are the only four positive at 100 ng/mL on all brands (tetrahydrofuranylfentanyl is (+) on One Step).
Recounted from Table 1 cell by cell.

reporting_issues.note: Recounted: the Negative row at 100 ng/mL (15, 19, 14, 13) includes the five unmeasured compounds.
My makers'-rule recount gives the same 20, 20, 19, 21 cumulative and 1, 2, 11, 4 at 100 ng/mL; the card's 18, 16, 14, 20 at 1000 ng/mL also checked.
Also not reconciled with the cross-reactivity data: the non-fentanyl drugs were tested only up to 1000 ng/mL, far below the mg/mL concentrations of an undiluted solution.

risk_of_bias.note: My own judgments match on all four domains (sample selection high, index test high, reference standard low, flow and timing unclear) and overall high.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor. Wording: results_show repeats 'carfentanil gave at most a faint band at 1000 ng/mL'. With competitive strips the band fades as the drug rises, so this reads backwards to many readers; 'no positive at 1000 ng/mL (a faint, ambiguous band on three brands, a solid band on One Step)' is clearer, and the same applies to cl_dc_fts_analogues.

missed: The replication timeline lists Sisco et al. (2024b) as not read and omits Halifax et al. (2024) and Lockwood et al. (2021), which are read in this round; where_it_stands could now cite them on carfentanil, analogue panels and high-concentration false positives.

Fig. 1C's lowest positive fentanyl readings (Rapid Response 50 ng/mL, One Step 25 ng/mL by the authors' rule) are on the card (key finding 1) but not in analysis.effect_sizes; the claim on fentanyl detection uses only Table 1's 100 ng/mL.
